'''Kotsuka Kofun''' (古津賀古墳) is a {{ill|Kofun|ca|Kofun|cs|Kofun|da|Kofun|de|Kofun|eo|Kofun|es|Kofun|fa|کوفون|fi|Kofun|fr|Kofun|he|קופון (רוגם)|hr|Kofun (grobnica)|it|Kofun|ja|古墳|ko|고훈|my|ခိုဖွန်း|pl|Kofun (kurhan)|pt|Kofun|ru|Кофун (захоронение)|simple|Kofun|th|โคฟุง|tr|Kofun|uk|Кофун|zh|古墳|qid=Q1141225|lt=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shimanto, Kōchi (city)|en|Shimanto, Kōchi (city)|qid=Q166946|lt=Shimanto}}, {{ill|Kōchi Prefecture|en|Kōchi Prefecture|qid=Q134093|lt=Kochi Prefecture}}, Japan. The mound is {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|simple|Round Kofun|zh|圓墳|qid=Q11394747|lt=round-shaped}} and has been designation1 as a Shimanto City Historic Site.

== Overview ==
Situated in western Kochi Prefecture, the Kofun is built on the slopes of a small hill (Mine-no-Mori) east of the former Nakamura city center. The name "Kotsuka" originates from "Kozuka" (old mound), and the nearby {{ill|Kotsuka Shrine|ja|古津賀神社|qid=Q140446008}} is said to have been founded as a site of worship for this kofun.<ref name="平凡社1983">{{Cite book|editor=|author=|year=1983|chapter=古津賀古墳|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 40 高知県の地名|publisher=[[Heibonsha]]|isbn=4582490409}}</ref> Archaeological excavations were conducted in {{ill|1962|en|1962|qid=Q2764|lt=1962}} and {{ill|1973|en|1973|qid=Q2477|lt=1973}} (Showa 37 and 48).<ref name="平凡社1983"/>

The mound is elliptical in type with a diameter of approximately 13 meters.<ref name="平凡社1983"/> The burial facility consists of a two-sleeved {{ill|stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} that opens southeastward. The total chamber length (corridor and main chamber) is 7.7 meters, making it the largest stone chamber in western Kochi Prefecture.<ref name="説明板"/> The chamber is constructed using siliceous sandstone, {{ill|Sandstone|en|Sandstone|qid=Q13085|lt=sandstone}}, and {{ill|Quartzite|en|Quartzite|qid=Q237883|lt=quartzite}}, likely sourced from the Tanogawa area in the midstream of the {{ill|Ushirogawa River|ja|後川|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q16766577}}.<ref name="平凡社1983"/> The chamber floor is lined with river stones collected from the Gogawa basin, and a wooden coffin was placed on top of these stones.<ref name="説明板"/> burial goods recovered from the chamber include burial goods, as described below.<ref name="平凡社1983"/>

The Kotsuka Kofun is estimated to have been constructed during the late {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}}, in the latter half of the {{ill|6th century|en|6th century|qid=Q8090|lt=6th century}}.<ref name="説明板"/> The scarcity of kofun in the Hata region highlights the significance of this site. The area is also recognized as the {{ill|Kotsuka Archaeological Site|ja|古津賀遺跡}}, where ritual burial goods related to river worship have been found in the floodplain of the Gogawa River.<ref>[https://sitereports.nabunken.go.jp/10282 『古津賀遺跡群 第1次-第6次発掘調査報告（四万十市文化財調査報告 第1輯）』] Shimanto City Board of Education, 2006.</ref>

In {{ill|1964|en|1964|qid=Q2652|lt=1964}} (Showa 39), the kofun site was designation1 as a historic site by the former Nakamura city government (now Shimanto City).<ref name="一覧"/><ref name="説明板"/>

== Excavation History ==
* Edo period: The mound was a site of worship, as evidenced by the discovery of {{ill|Kan'ei Tsūhō|en|Kan'ei Tsūhō|qid=Q11457504|lt=Kan'ei Tsūhō}} coins and Haji pottery during investigations.<ref name="平凡社1983"/>
* {{ill|1962|en|1962|qid=Q2764|lt=1962}}: First excavation.<ref name="平凡社1983"/>
* {{ill|1964|en|1964|qid=Q2652|lt=1964}}: Designated as a historic site by Nakamura City.<ref name="一覧"/><ref name="説明板"/>
* {{ill|1973|en|1973|qid=Q2477|lt=1973}}: Second excavation; first restoration.<ref name="説明板"/>
* {{ill|1974|en|1974|qid=Q2478|lt=1974}}: Second restoration.<ref name="説明板"/>

== burial goods ==
Significant burial goods excavated include the following:<ref name="高知県2009">{{Cite book|editor=|author=|year=2009|chapter=|title=[https://sitereports.nabunken.go.jp/10247 高知県後期古墳資料集I（高知大学考古学調査研究報告 第7冊）]|publisher=Kochi University Archaeology Research Lab}}</ref>
* Two gold rings
* One iron sword
* One belt decoration
* Over 15 iron arrowheads
* More than three knives

The burial goods are preserved and displayed at the Shimanto Municipal Museum of Local History (Shimanto City, Nakamura).<ref name="説明板"/>
